scope: Run the preplanned US 23-Nov suppression scheme unchanged against the corrected Branch-B hardened base network; stop before US adaptive reallocation.
rules: US plan and target priorities are held fixed for Pass A.
Japanese D-1 warning/dispersion already earned by the contact chain is active.
Hardening is resolved by target layer; no flat base-survival multiplier.
Aircraft may evacuate/stage if warning, fuel, runway and destination permit; this costs sortie/maintenance state.

Nauru_Wasp_Princeton.offensive_sorties: ~100-125 across fighter sweep/escort and attack cycles
Nauru_Wasp_Princeton.note: Historical Nauru all-day scale used only as workload sanity anchor; Branch carrier identity/date follow current v048.

outer_Marshalls_fast_carrier_suppression.priority: Taroa first; Mili/Jaluit next; Wotje/Kwaj support/C2 as geometry permits

land_based_Dminus1.effective_bomber_attack_sorties: ~24-36 against Tarawa/Makin and selected southern nodes

Nauru.runway: daylight operations heavily suppressed; multiple craters; no normal-cycle sortie generation

Maloelap_Taroa.ready_center_band: 21-27 total after fixed suppression; fighters ~14-19, attack 3-5, recon/Zuiun 2-3
Maloelap_Taroa.runway: heavily cratered but repair parties preserve intermittent strip/taxi use by late day
Maloelap_Taroa.base_system: C2/fuel/workshop materially damaged but not collapsed; P2/P3 dispersion prevents several cluster kills
Maloelap_Taroa.Raiden: surviving detachment remains material but pays CAP/interception attrition

Mili.ready_center_band: 18-23 total; attack aircraft ~9-11 remain the strongest dusk strike reservoir
Mili.runway: degraded but usable in windows after repair
Mili.water_air: Kyofu/Zuiun layer largely persists unless individually found

Wotje.system: suppressed but not closed; revetments/stores force repeat work

Jaluit.system: land strip damaged; lagoon search/intercept layer persists because ramp/fuel/comms are separate targets

Kwajalein_Roi_Ebeye.system: larger network and lower D-1 strike priority preserve command/search/logistics continuity

Tarawa_Betio_air.decision: evacuate a useful fraction of flyable nonessential aircraft once invasion scale is unmistakable; do not sacrifice every serviceable machine on Betio
Tarawa_Betio_air.evacuated_by_late_23: ~7-10 fighters plus 1-2 attack/recon aircraft to Mili/Jaluit/Marshall staging if individually serviceable
Tarawa_Betio_air.local_ready_after_Dminus1: ~2-5 fighters and 0-1 attack/recon in a severely suppressed runway environment
Tarawa_Betio_air.effect: aircraft survival transfers to regional wallet; it does not make Betio an active D-Day airbase

regional_effect.attack_aircraft_available_for_dusk_marit: ~22-26 after fixed ground suppression and staging, consistent with but slightly more robust than old ~22-sortie line
regional_effect.fighter_search_water_air: material residual network survives; US cannot treat first sweep as regional sterilization

historical_sanity_anchors: Historical GALVANIC fast carriers attacked Marshalls while a separate carrier group struck Nauru; historical Nauru attack was an all-day multi-cycle effort.
Historical Tarawa pre-invasion week used repeated land-based bombing; fixed Pass A preserves equivalent operational intent, not exact Branch routing or ship identity.
